title: The curated-deps marker outlived the site-packages it described - every engine upgrade shipped 5 dead node packs
description: ensureCuratedPythonDeps() stamped its marker at ENGINE_ROOT/.cubric_python_deps, but the full reinstall in /engine/upgrade removes ENGINE_ROOT/<COMFY_DIR>, which on Windows CONTAINS python_embeded/Lib/site-packages. The marker sat one level up and survived the thing it was a claim about, so the next /comfy/start read a matching hash and skipped the install. ComfyUI then booted with No module named cv2 / pywt and comfyui_controlnet_aux, RES4LYF, Impact-Pack, Impact-Subpack and LTXVideo all IMPORT FAILED - 17 shipped class_types gone, no error surfaced, failure deferred to whenever the user next ran a graph needing one. Same shape as MPI-465. Until MPI-457 added the in-place path, the wipe was the ONLY upgrade route, so every user who upgraded the engine landed here. Found by actually RUNNING the upgrade (MPI-457 acceptance 5); no unit test could have reached it.
acceptance: The marker shares the fate of the site-packages it describes - anchored on getPythonBin(), never ENGINE_ROOT
Correct on BOTH platforms for the same reason: Windows inside the portable (wipe takes it), Linux/macOS inside comfy-venv (wipe does not, and the deps really do survive)
A test pins the placement so it cannot drift back
Proven live: floor check 17 missing -> 0 after a real wipe + reinstall + start cycle
